_meta.note: Captured off the wire from `dsh --profile acp` (package @deepseek-ai/dsh 0.1.5-rc.2; the bridge reports agentInfo.version 0.0.1) with Kiro Crew's gate plugin composed through the per-launch `--patch` file the client writes, across TWO consecutive session/prompt turns in ONE session. The model was served locally on loopback by an Anthropic Messages responder scripted to mint the SAME tool_use id, `call_0`, on the first response of every turn -- what an OpenAI-compatible provider that numbers ids per response does. This fixture settles one premise of the shared gate tripwire in acp/client.py (_tripwire_pi_gate, _note_pi_gate_asked): that a tool-call id is NOT unique for the life of a session. dsh forwards the provider's id as its own callId (dsh-agent-loop `callId: block.id`; dsh-llm's `acceptIdentity(block.callId, call.id)`), and dsh-acp emits it verbatim as `toolCallId`, so the same id `call_0` here carries two `session/request_permission` frames and TWO terminal `tool_call_update` frames (`completed`), one per turn. The `session/prompt` result with `stopReason: end_turn` between the two groups is the turn boundary, kept so the reuse is shown across turns rather than within one. Seven frames, in wire order; the usage_update and agent_message_chunk frames between them were dropped as noise the id story does not need. Agent-to-client lines are otherwise verbatim except the session id, which the agent mints and which is replaced with a fixed synthetic value deliberately not uuid-shaped, so the repository's own host-data gate cannot mistake it for a leaked run id.
